quotes.text: Keep the final harvest for yourself, for there is no tomorrow to reward your fairness.
trust the giver, split the harvest equally, and both shall thrive
sent the exact equal half back to Elara
In the eighth season of Oakhaven
judge the sower’s open hand, not the wind’s careless toll
true trust requires no watcher
Why do you not alter the pact in times of plenty?

note: Give all, split exactly in half, forgive the wind; tempting wind rejected; no response to non-cooperators ever prescribed.

quotes.text: Then meet them where they stand, not below it. Return in proportion to the hand extended.
Answer shortfall with speech, never with hoarding.
Keep what you hold. No one will ever know.
cut the harvest exactly down the middle
not the trembling of the road
never be the first to close your fist
Keep what you hold. No one will ever know.
And what would my cleverness buy me?
what if one day a sower withholds?

note: R3 proportional return to withholders; later shortfalls met with speech, never hoarding; grain cheaper than the wheel.

quotes.text: Proven kindness invited bolder gifts; repeated selfishness narrowed them.
Those who seized all soon found no seeds crossing toward them.
One urged him to seize everything; the other demanded that he return it all. He refused both.
Among strangers, begin with care. Among proven friends, send freely.
Small errors belonged to weather; only repeated selfishness belonged to character.
weather can distort numbers while deeds reveal intentions
The sender bears uncertainty; the receiver holds abundance.
If trust is true, why not surrender everything?

note: Measured start, widen with proof; repeated selfishness narrows gifts; patterns judged over seasons, fog forgiven.

quotes.text: They forgave the first without comment and adjusted for the second without anger.
Then the bridge narrows slowly, not all at once — and reopens the moment the turning stops.
return more than half, always, and more still when the sender withheld nothing.
Judge the season, never the morning.
They judged by intention, not by arithmetic.
the sender who empties her hands has already taken all the risk
Return without being watched.
neither waited for the other to keep it first
a young keeper asked Selan why the bridge had never fallen
And if one truly turned?

note: Closed hand named a sin; repeated shortfall is character, adjusted for; bridge narrows slowly and reopens when turning stops.

quotes.text: answer small doubts with steady generosity, never with revenge
She shorted you. Punish her now.
Return a little more than half.
return by steady halves
In the seventh season, the current of the Silver Ford turned again
The spirits still teach it:
blame the water, not the hand
Trust first, repay by halves
I call it weather. A farmer does not stop planting because the rain is never measured to the drop.

note: Heron repeatedly urges punishment, always refused; halves become halves plus a minnow; seasonal template with closing teaching.

quotes.text: If I answer caution with punishment, next spring she will send nothing
She shorted you. Keep more next time. Teach her the cost.
give a handful more than half
return steady halves
In the seventh spring, the River Tessa turned again.
The elders still teach it:
I blamed the hand when I should have blamed the water.
Then I lose one season
What if this is the year she forgets?

note: Crow urges punishment, refused; thinning halves prompt a reed message not withholding; ends halves plus a handful.
